 What is a criminal profile, and how does it affect you in GTA 6?

 GTA 6 's criminal profiles (plural, because Jason and Lucia each have their own criminal profile) tracks how you treat other people in the world, reminiscent of Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system. How violent you are, how lethal you are in your encounters, and how you treat people and animals in the world will all affect your rating.
 Criminal Profile levels 
 (Image credit: Rockstar) There are five levels for Jason and Lucia's criminal profile, represented by "face with horns" emoji-style icons that are shown on your screen:
 Professional (yellow icon)
 Hardened (orange icon)
 Violent (purple icon)
 Psycho (light gray icon)
 Irredeemable (dark gray icon)
 How Criminal Profiles work 
 (Image credit: Rockstar) Your criminal profile is almost entirely dependent on how often you kill people . Try to incapacitate enemies, or wound them instead of killing them, and don't kill too many police or civilians, and you'll wind up with a Professional or Hardened profile. If you're violent for no reason, kill a lot of cops and civilians, and kill pets or defenseless animals, you'll gain a Violent, Psycho, or Irredeemable profile.
 Latest Videos From PC Gamer Watch full video here: Here are the behaviors that will grant you each of the criminal profiles, and the bonuses that come with them:
 Professional 
 Keep the violence to what is strictly necessary
 Avoid casualties when possible by incapacitating enemies instead of killing them
 Go undetected whenever possible
 Bonus: Non-lethal incapacitations and thoughtful acts to citizens will increase your focus meter (bullet-time)

 Hardened
 Kill enemies
 Kill citizens (in self-defense)
 Don't worry about detection
 Bonus: Non-lethal incapacitations and thoughtful acts to citizens will increase your focus meter (same as Professional)
 Violent
 Ignore non-lethal options
 Kill enemies and police
 Kill citizens indiscriminately
 Bonus: Headshots will increase your focus meter

 Killing lots of cops
 Killing helpless citizens regularly
 Killing domestic and defenseless animals (doesn't apply to hunting)
 Bonus: Headhosts will increase your focus meter, but you will be unable to surrender to cops
 Irredeemable
 If you're a Psycho for too long, you'll gain the Irredeemable profile. While you can move up and down between the other four profiles during the game, once you have an Irredeemable criminal profile, it's permanent .
 According to Rockstar, "being irredeemable will have a lasting impact on Jason and Lucia," though we don't yet know what that means. We'll update this guide when we find out.

 My stats for Professional 
 (Image credit: Rockstar) For my playthrough of the main story, I typically kept both Jason and Lucia in the Professional range, which is the profile I finished the main story with, though I did occasionally drop both of them down to Hardened.
 I did this by (mostly) trying to be non-lethal in my encounters, using focus to aim for my enemies' knees and elbows during shootouts. I still killed a whole mess of people in my playthrough.

 *A note on that animal total: I did a little bit of hunting, and I once ran over a cat (by accident!). But most of those animal kills, I suspect, are birds, which have some of the worst AI I've ever seen in a game. They do not get out of the way of cars, trucks, boats, planes, helicopters, ATVs, scooters, and even bicycles. You are going to run over a lot of birds. Sorry.

 Chris started playing PC games in the 1980s, started writing about them in the early 2000s, and (finally) started getting paid to write about them in the late 2000s. Following a few years as a regular freelancer, PC Gamer hired him in 2014, probably so he'd stop emailing them asking for more work.
